TruncatedLinearRegression.summary: Truncated linear regression ``y = w^T x + b + e``, ``e ~ N(0, sigma^2)``.
TruncatedLinearRegression.docstring:
Truncated linear regression ``y = w^T x + b + e``, ``e ~ N(0, sigma^2)``.

Observed only where ``phi(y)`` admits it. The variant follows the
arguments, as an OLS package's would: a known ``noise_var``, an unknown
one, or dependent data.

attributes.noise_var: The known noise variance, or None when it is learned.
attributes.dependent: Whether the samples come from one trajectory.
attributes.survival_threshold: The s dividing dependent data's ``Sigma_0``; 1 otherwise.

params.name: phi
params.description: Truncation oracle over responses shaped (n, m, k).

params.name: alpha
params.description: Survival probability in (0, 1]; None if unknown, which dependent data does not support.

params.name: noise_var
params.description: The known noise variance; None learns it, training ``weight`` as ``(v, lambda)``: v's rows, then lambda's.

params.name: dependent
params.description: Whether each row of X is a state x_t and its row of y the next state x_{t+1}, both observed, the rows in temporal order; needs noise_var, the noise covariance, and alpha, a lower bound on ``P(x_{t+1} in S | x_t)``.

params.name: sampler
params.description: Estimates the loss's conditional moments; rejection sampling at ``num_samples`` and ``min_accepted`` by default. Unused for dependent data, whose test draws a fixed number.

params.name: emp_weight
params.description: Start in place of OLS; see ``TruncatedLinearModel``.

params.name: rand_seed
params.description: Seed applied at the start of every run.

raises.ValueError: If dependent data lacks noise_var or alpha.

methods.name: coefficients
methods.summary: Split a flat iterate; for learned variance, ``(v, lambda)``.

methods.name: confidence_intervals
methods.summary: Return Wald intervals for the coefficients, intercept and variance.

methods.name: covariance
methods.summary: Return the asymptotic covariance of an estimate.

methods.name: fit
methods.summary: Fit the model, with y divided by OLS's residual sd when learning it.

methods.name: hessian
methods.summary: Return the NLL's mean Hessian over the data, by default at the iterate.

methods.name: predict
methods.summary: Return ``h_W(x)`` at ``coef_`` and ``intercept_``, shaped (n, k).

methods.name: refine
methods.summary: Take the Newton steps, which carry their own curvature, unpreconditioned.

methods.name: summary
methods.summary: Return a plain-text report on the fit.

methods.name: variance
methods.summary: Return the noise variance at a flat iterate, shaped (k,).

TruncatedLassoRegression.docstring:
Truncated lasso regression ``y = w^T x + b + e``, ``e ~ N(0, sigma^2)``.

Observed only where ``phi(y)`` admits it, with sigma^2 known. The
intercept is not penalized.

attributes.l1: The penalty, on the coefficients of ``y / sqrt(noise_var)``; None until fit when left to the default.
attributes.intercept_column: The design matrix's intercept column, the rows' root mean square norm rather than 1, so the one step size suits the intercept as well as the coefficients.

params.name: phi
params.description: Truncation oracle over responses shaped (n, m, 1).

params.name: alpha
params.description: Survival probability in (0, 1], or None if unknown.

params.name: l1
params.description: The penalty on the coefficients of ``y / sqrt(noise_var)``; ``sqrt(log(d) / n)`` if None.

params.name: sampler
params.description: Estimates the loss's conditional moments; rejection sampling at ``num_samples`` and ``min_accepted`` by default.

params.name: fit_intercept
params.description: Whether to fit an unpenalized intercept.

params.name: emp_weight
params.description: Start in place of the smallest-L1 point of E_r; see ``TruncatedLinearModel``.

params.name: rand_seed
params.description: Seed applied at the start of every run.

raises.ValueError: If l1 or noise_var is not positive.

methods.name: fit
methods.summary: Fit the model to y divided by the noise's standard deviation.

methods.name: hessian

Truncated multinomial logistic regression over labels 0, ..., K - 1.

``coef_`` and ``intercept_`` hold classes 1 to K - 1, shaped (K - 1, d)
and (K - 1,); class 0's are zero. ``phi`` sees latents shaped
(n, m, K), and alpha is at most 1 / K.

The descent is unconstrained: no analysis yet shows that the
multinomial needs R_alpha, so alpha sets no projection set.
